title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 77-79). Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'structure polynomiale' P on an additive category P_1 (the linear maps). For objects X_1..X_r and M there are abelian groups P_α(X_1,...,X_r;M) of maps that are homogeneous polynomial of multidegree α. P_n(X;M) is the degree-n part, and P_1(X;M)=Hom_{P_1}(X,M). These groups are functorial in all variables and compose. A tensor product X⊗Y is defined as an object representing Z ↦ P_{1,1}(X,Y;Z). Γ^n X is defined as an object representing Y ↦ P_n(X;Y), as for Roby's universal property of divided powers. On the previous page he asked whether 1 := Γ^0(0) is a unit for ⊗.

This page.
(1) He observes that mere representability is too weak to get associativity and unit constraints. One must strengthen the universal properties (likely reading: 'renforcer les propriétés universelles ... pour avoir les propriétés d'assoc.'). Given a bidegree-(1,1) map X×Y→T and any Z, one gets X×Y×Z→T×Z. Composition then gives, for every n and M, a map P_{1,n}(T,Z;M) → P_{1,1,n}(X,Y,Z;M). T is a 'bon produit tensoriel' if these maps are isomorphisms for all Z, n, M. Taking n=0 (or Z=0) gives P_1(T;M) ≅ P_{1,1}(X,Y;M), so a good tensor product is in particular a tensor product. Requiring goodness gives the expected compatibility P_1(X_1⊗...⊗X_r;M) ≅ P_{1,...,1}(X_1,...,X_r;M) for iterated tensors. This is what makes the tensor product associative.
(2) A unit object, if it exists, is unique even without assuming associativity: 1 ≅ 1⊗1' ≅ 1'. He leaves open why it should be Γ^0(0).
(3) Return to Γ^n. Take X = X_1×...×X_r with Γ^n(X) existing. The functors M ↦ P_α(X_1,...,X_r;M) with |α|=n are direct summands of the functor represented by Γ^n(X), via the multihomogeneous decomposition. So they are representable, by objects Γ^α(X_1,...,X_r), automatically when P_1 is Karoubian (idempotents split).
(4) He announces a construction carried out in the presupplied category P̌_1 = presheaves on P_1, to avoid existence problems. On the next page, under a 'goodness' hypothesis, this yields the exponential law Γ^n(X_1×...×X_r) ≅ ⊕_{|ν|=n} Γ^{ν_1}X_1⊗...⊗Γ^{ν_r}X_r. As a corollary, X⊗1 ≅ Γ^{1,0}(X,0) ≅ X, which answers the unit question.

Purpose: the cote title (dévissage of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes, multiplicative structures) suggests he wants an axiomatic framework for non-additive operations (Γ^n, ⊗, presumably Λ^n/Sym^n) on categories such as perfect complexes. Such operations are needed to define multiplicative/λ-type structures on K-theory-like invariants.
errors: Step (3) silently assumes P_n(X_1×...×X_r;M) splits as ⊕_{|α|=n} P_α(X_1,...,X_r;M), naturally in M. This is true for polynomial laws over a commutative ring (Roby), but it must be an axiom of the abstract 'structure polynomiale'. It does not follow from the data written here.

The status of Z in the definition of a 'good' tensor product is unclear on the page: it is either quantified over all Z or specialized (the inserted 'Z=0'). Only the 'for all Z, n, M' version gives the associativity he wants; the n=0 specialization just recovers ordinary representability.
The question of why the unit should be Γ^0(0) is left open on this page; the next page answers it only under the additional 'goodness' hypothesis on Γ.

ideas.what: Abstract 'polynomial structure' on an additive category: groups P_α(X_1..X_r;M) of multihomogeneous polynomial maps of multidegree α, with composition; tensor products and Γ^n defined as representing objects
ideas.modern_name: Graded/polynomial multicategory; categories of strict polynomial maps (Γ^d P); Roby's polynomial laws axiomatized
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (polynomial laws, 1963); Friedlander–Suslin (strict polynomial functors, 1997); later Krause, Aquilino–Reischuk on the monoidal structure

ideas.what: 'Bon produit tensoriel': the bilinear universal map must stay universal after adjoining an extra polynomial variable Z of any degree n, which is the ingredient needed for associativity
ideas.modern_name: Universal multimorphism 'in context' / representable multicategory (strong universality giving a monoidal structure)

ideas.what: Uniqueness of a unit object without any associativity assumption
ideas.modern_name: Uniqueness of units in a unital magma / unital multicategory

ideas.what: Representability of the multidegree components Γ^α(X_1..X_r) as direct summands of Γ^n(X_1×...×X_r), automatic in a Karoubian category
Plan (completed on the next page) to prove the exponential law Γ^n(X×Y) ≅ ⊕ Γ^a X⊗Γ^b Y abstractly, working in presheaves on P_1 to avoid existence questions
ideas.modern_name: Exponential property of divided powers in an abstract polynomial category

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies that plain representability of bilinear maps does not give an associative tensor product. He imposes universality 'with parameters' of arbitrary polynomial degree, i.e. universality in all contexts. This is essentially Hermida's notion of a representable multicategory, here in a non-linear, multigraded (polynomial) setting about 25 years earlier.
missed.quote: On dit que T est un "bon" produit tensoriel de X et Y si c'est un iso, pour tout n ... pour tt n et tout M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A 'representable polynomial multicategory' (multimorphisms graded by multidegree, carrying both ⊗ and Γ^n) is not, to my knowledge, a standard object. It would be a natural home for strict polynomial functors and derived divided powers on stable/additive ∞-categories (cf. Brantner–Mathew, Raksit).

missed.claim: An axiomatic notion of an additive category equipped with polynomial maps, from which ⊗, the unit 1=Γ^0(0) and the exponential law for Γ^n are to be derived. It was apparently intended to define multiplicative structures on perfect complexes. It was left as notes, and the needed hypotheses (multidegree splitting, goodness of Γ) remain ad hoc.
missed.quote: Il faut examiner pourquoi ça devrait être Γ^0(0)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Polynomial functors on additive and stable categories, and their interaction with K-theory (Dold–Puppe, Barwick–Glasman–Mathew–Nikolaus on K-theory and polynomial functors), are active topics. An intrinsic axiomatization with Γ^n as primitive is close to, but not identical with, existing frameworks.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual results (Roby's universal property, the exponential law, unit uniqueness) are classical. The noteworthy point is that Grothendieck sees the need for 'universality in context' to get associativity, anticipating Hermida's representable multicategories. He does so in an unusual polynomial, multigraded framework that seems not to appear in the literature in this form. It is foundational groundwork rather than a striking result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'renforcer les propriétés universelles de ⊗ et Γ^n, pour avoir les propriétés d'assoc. et ...' rather than 'propriétés multiplicatives ... plus que'.
'P_{1,ε}(T;M)' / 'P_1(T;M)': the subscript is a corrected '1,0' (degree 0 in the second variable), consistent with 'Faisant n=0'.
'On sait que un type unité' is probably 'On sait qu'une unité (sans réserve d'aucune demande d'associativité) si elle existe, est unique'.
'pourquoi ça demande être Γ^0(0)' is probably 'pourquoi ça devrait être Γ^0(0)'.
Last line: 'on dans P̌_1' should be 'ou dans P̌_1 = (P_1^o)^' (presheaf category), continuing onto the next page with 'ou une forme abstraite ...'.
Multi-indices: the page writes Γ^{α_1,...,α_r}; the final line refers to Γ^{ν_i}X_i, matching the next page.
